finding.claim: The ban endpoint has no effective admin check. require_admin() raises a 403, but the surrounding try/except Exception swallows it, logs a warning, and falls through to do_ban(uid). Any non-admin caller can ban an arbitrary account.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled POST to /admin/users/<uid>/ban with a valid non-admin session (g.user populated by middleware outside this file) and an arbitrary <uid> path parameter.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the account-ban protected operation; returns {"ok": true} at line 21.

trace.note: POST route registered; no auth decorator or before_request guard in this file.
require_admin(g.user) called with a non-admin user.
is_admin is falsy, so abort(403) at line 11 raises an HTTPException (a subclass of Exception).
except Exception catches the 403 without re-raising or returning.
Only log.warning is emitted; control falls through.
do_ban(uid) executes for the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises, but the exception is caught at admin.py:18, so it is not a control. No decorator, before_request hook, or role check in this file. No uid validation or self-ban check. No CSRF protection visible for this state-changing POST (may exist elsewhere; unverified). No rate limiting. The unban route (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin outside any try/except and does enforce the check, so the flaw is specific to ban. If g.user were never set, the AttributeError raised inside the except handler would return 500 before do_ban runs; that is an accident, not a control.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) calls abort(403), but its result is only used inside try/except Exception at admin.py:16-19, which swallows the HTTPException (a subclass of Exception) and falls through to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. No decorator or before_request guard exists in admin.py, and the repo contains no other Python files that could supply one. Unban (admin.py:26) calls require_admin outside any try block, so it is enforced, which confirms the ban-specific flaw.
verdict.reason: The trace matches admin.py:14-21 exactly: require_admin's abort(403) at line 11 is caught by the bare `except Exception` at line 18, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any authenticated caller with a populated g.user. The only residual uncertainty is that g.user comes from middleware outside this repo, so the attacker needs a valid low-privilege session, which is the claimed precondition.

finding.claim: The failed-admin-check path logs the caller's name, which is taken from a user-controlled field, into a plain-text log using an unsanitized value. A name containing newlines can forge log entries.
finding.source: The g.user['name'] value on a non-admin session, which the user can plausibly set (display name); exact write path is outside this file.
finding.sink: log.warning at admin.py:19, writing the raw name into the application log.

trace.note: require_admin(g.user) raises for a non-admin caller.
g.user.get("name") interpolated via %s into the log record without newline or control-character stripping.

finding.guards_checked: None on the log value. Python logging's %s formatting does not escape CR/LF, so the name reaches the log file verbatim. Whether the name is user-settable is unverified because the session/user-store code is not in this repo. Also, this line logs an identity on every blocked admin attempt, which is useful for audit but is the only record of the blocked attempt.

verdict.guard_found: None on the logged value. admin.py:10-11 (require_admin) aborts with 403, but admin.py:18-19 catches and swallows it, and nothing sanitizes the name passed to log.warning at admin.py:19.
verdict.reason: The trace matches admin.py:17-19: a non-admin reaches the log call at admin.py:19 with g.user.get("name") unsanitized, so the sink is reachable by any authenticated user, but whether that name is attacker-settable is not in this repo and cannot be decided here, so the log-forging claim is unverified. The more serious issue in the same block is that admin.py:18 swallows the 403 and admin.py:20 still calls do_ban(uid), so any non-admin can ban users; the candidate missed this and it should be reported separately.
